title: Packaging as a jar, a container image and shipping it

videos.script: Twenty-two lessons built the bookshop. It runs on your machine, from a terminal, against your database. {{laptop}} A server is not your machine. It has no Maven, no source code, and no idea what your password is. {{server}} This lesson packages the bookshop so that it runs anywhere with Java, or anywhere with Docker. {{ship}} First you open the jar that Maven builds. A hundred and twelve libraries live inside it, and a small launcher knows how to read them. {{jar}} Then the password leaves the project's files. The environment hands it in when the jar starts. {{env}} You split the jar into four layers, sorted by how often they change. {{layers}} A Dockerfile turns those layers into an image. You change one line of code, build again, and watch Docker keep the sixty-nine megabytes it already had. {{cache}} Compose starts the bookshop beside a PostgreSQL of its own, with one command. {{compose}} And you stop it the way a server stops it, and watch it finish its work before it exits. {{stop}}
